prompt: As a user types, suggest up to three dictionary words that start with the typed prefix.
why: Walk the trie one letter per keystroke; the subtree under the node holds every match.
trap: Binary search over sorted words also works, but a trie reuses work between keystrokes.

prompt: Design a word store that supports adding words and searching patterns where '.' matches any letter.
why: Store words in a trie; on '.', branch into every child.
trap: Scanning every word for every search ignores the shared prefixes.

prompt: Find every word from a list of 10,000 words that can be traced in a letter grid.
tells: every word from a list of 10,000 words
why: Put all words in a trie and run one backtracking search that follows the trie, pruning dead prefixes.
trap: Backtracking once per word repeats the same grid walks 10,000 times.

prompt: Given a dictionary of word roots, replace every word in a sentence with the shortest root it starts with.
why: Walk each word down the trie and stop at the first node that ends a root.
trap: Checking every prefix against a set works but rebuilds strings each time.

prompt: Find the maximum XOR of any two numbers in an array of 200,000 integers.
tells: maximum XOR of any two numbers
why: Insert numbers bit by bit into a binary trie; for each number, greedily walk the opposite bit.
trap: Sorting doesn't order XOR results; the bits need a trie.
